finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test sends a server-side request to a fully attacker-chosen URL with no validation. Attackers can reach internal services and cloud metadata endpoints, and can learn the response status.

trace.note: pub router has no auth middleware
upstream status returned to the caller, giving a response oracle

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or IP allowlist, no private-range block, no DNS pinning. axios follows redirects by default. requireAdmin is applied only to the admin router (line 12), not to pub.

verdict.reason: routes.js:20 passes req.body.callback straight into axios.post on the pub router (routes.js:4, no auth middleware; requireAdmin is only applied to admin at routes.js:12), with no validation, and routes.js:21 returns the upstream status; routes.js is the only file, so no mounting middleware can add a guard.

finding.claim: Admin diagnostics endpoint fetches an arbitrary URL from the query string with no destination validation. Any admin, or a hijacked admin session, can reach internal networks and metadata services. Severity is lower because the endpoint is admin-gated.

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) gates the router on session role
upstream status returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (lines 7-10) restricts access to admin sessions only. There is no URL, host or IP validation, and redirects are followed.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied at routes.js:12) blocks non-admin sessions with a 403. It is an authorization gate, not URL validation. No destination validation exists.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: routes.js:15 passes req.query.url straight to axios.get. But the whole admin router is gated by requireAdmin at routes.js:8-12, so only admin sessions can supply the value and no unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker can reach the sink.
